I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`. No lodash import is left.

- **`doubled`:** it uses `mapValues` from `es-toolkit`, with the same callback.
- **`byNameKey`:** it uses `keyBy` from `es-toolkit`. That version takes a function rather than a property name, so I added the adapter `(row) => row.name`.
- **`isBlank`:** it uses `isEmpty` from `es-toolkit/compat`. The core `es-toolkit` build only has `isEmptyObject`, which doesn't cover the lodash `isEmpty` cases in your input range: `null`, booleans, numbers, strings and arrays. So I kept the compat version.

`npm run size -- out/module.ts` prints 636 bytes (min+gzip) and 95 bytes of own code. Importing from the subpaths `es-toolkit/object` and `es-toolkit/array` came out at 639 bytes, so I kept the root import.

I couldn't compare against the original or check that results match it. `lodash` isn't installed, so `src/module.ts` doesn't build and `npm run size` fails on it. `tsc` reports no errors for `out/module.ts`. It only reports the missing `lodash` imports (and the implicit `any` they cause) in `src/module.ts`. I didn't run any input-equivalence tests. The `isEmpty` choice rests on the lodash behaviour I know for your input range.

The exports, `Row` and `Config` are unchanged. I removed my two temporary size-test files, so `out/` contains only `module.ts`.
